scripts.radio:
Good evening, listeners. You are tuned to Kenya on Record, where we keep watch on public interest, security, and our national heritage.

First, a serious warning about your digital footprint. Online conmen are no longer relying on faceless accounts. Instead, they are systematically harvesting photos of ordinary Kenyans from social media to create duplicate profiles. These fake accounts are used to infiltrate communities, build trust, and pitch fraudulent business schemes or urgent financial distress calls. Before you send money to anyone claiming to be a friend, an investor, or an old classmate, stop and verify. Demand a phone call, insist on a face-to-face meeting, and never commit funds solely based on a familiar picture.

On a positive note, Lake Nakuru National Park continues to set a benchmark in wildlife protection. Covering 188 square kilometres of securely fenced sanctuary, the park provides critical refuge to both black and white rhinos. In an era where poaching and habitat fragmentation threaten our biodiversity, the sustained, disciplined management at Nakuru demonstrates what institutional accountability can achieve for our national heritage.

Kwa ufupi: Kuweni waangalifu mitandaoni. Matapeli wanatumia picha za watu halisi kutengeneza akaunti feki ili kuwaibia wananchi pesa. Hakikisha utambulisho wa mtu kabla ya kutuma fedha. Wakati huo huo, Hifadhi ya Ziwa Nakuru inaendelea kulinda vifaru weusi na weupe kwa ufanisi mkubwa katika eneo lililolindwa la kilomita za mraba 188.

Stay sharp, protect your savings, and value our heritage.
scripts.voice_note:
Habari zenu. This is Kenya on Record with a quick briefing you should share with family this week.

Be very vigilant on WhatsApp, Facebook, and Instagram. Scammers are copying photos and details of real people to build believable profiles, pretending to be professionals, trusted peers, or old friends in need of urgent help. Once trust is established, the trap closes and money is lost. Please, if anyone approaches you online asking for funds or pitching deals, verify them through a direct phone call before sending a single shilling.

On conservation, Lake Nakuru National Park is demonstrating real impact. Its 188-square-kilometre fenced sanctuary continues to provide tight, round-the-clock protection for both black and white rhinos. Sound management yields real results.

Protect your digital space, stay informed, and have a safe, productive week ahead.
scripts.sms: USIIBIWE: Scammers steal photos of real people to create fake profiles and solicit cash. Always verify identities via a direct phone call before sending money.
scripts.reels:
That friendly profile asking for an emergency loan or offering an investment deal might not be who you think. 

Conmen are scraping photos of everyday Kenyans to create fake profiles, build your trust, and trap your money. If you have only met someone through a screen, pause. Insist on a video call, verify their contacts, and do not send money to strangers. 

A clean profile picture is not proof of character.
